rows.question: Where does Northstar Analytics have offices?
rows.answer: Northstar Analytics has offices in Toronto, Montreal, and New York.

retrieved_chunks.content_preview:
Company Overview

Northstar Analytics builds analytics and workflow automation software for operations teams in finance, healthcare operations, logistics, and professional services. Employees are expected to protect customer trust, communicate clearly, and make decisions that improve operational reliability.

Northstar has offices in Toronto, Montreal, and New York. The company supports hybrid work and approved remote work across Canada and the United States.

Work Model

Northstar supports hybrid work and approved remote work. Employees assigned to Toronto, Montreal, or New York offices are expected to attend office collaboration days when scheduled by their department.

Remote employees may work from approved locations in Canada or the United States if their role, tax location, and security requirements support remote work.

Company Holidays

Northstar observes 11 company holidays each year. Holiday calendars may vary by employee location. Employees should follow the holiday calendar assigned to their work location in the HR system.

Company Values

Northstar's operating values are clarity, ownership, evidence, and trust. Employees should make decisions with evidence, document important work, and raise risks early. Teams are expected to treat internal policies as source-of-truth guidance rather than informal suggestions.

Health Benefits

Northstar provides health, dental, and vision benefits to eligible full-time employees. Coverage begins on the first day of the month after the employee's start date. Plan details vary by employee location.

This overview does not include provider contracts, claim adjudication rules, or legal advice about benefits eligibility.

rows.question: How many paid vacation days do full-time employees receive each calendar year?
rows.answer: Full-time employees receive 20 paid vacation days per calendar year.

citations.citation_text: Full-time employees receive 20 paid vacation days per calendar year.
citations.source: Source: HR-002 PTO and Leave Policy, Section: Vacation Entitlement

retrieved_chunks.content_preview:
Vacation Entitlement

Full-time employees receive 20 paid vacation days per calendar year. Vacation is accrued monthly and may be used after the employee's first 30 days of employment. Part-time employees receive prorated vacation based on scheduled weekly hours.

Employees may carry over up to 5 unused vacation days into the next calendar year. Carried-over days must be used by March 31 or they expire unless local law requires a different outcome.

Sick Leave

Employees receive 8 paid sick days per calendar year. Sick time may be used for personal illness, medical appointments, or short-term caregiving needs. Employees should notify their manager as soon as practical when taking sick leave.

Medical details should not be shared in team channels. People Operations may request documentation only when required by policy or law.

Parental Leave Summary

Eligible full-time employees may receive up to 12 weeks of company-supported parental leave after 6 months of service. Local statutory benefits may apply separately. Employees should contact People Operations at least 60 days before the expected leave date when possible.

This document provides a company policy summary and does not provide legal advice.

Vacation Approval Workflow

Vacation requests of 1 to 5 business days should be submitted at least 10 business days in advance. Requests longer than 5 business days should be submitted at least 20 business days in advance.

Managers approve vacation based on business coverage, project deadlines, and fairness across the team. Managers should not deny vacation without explaining the business reason.

Company Holidays

Northstar observes 11 company holidays each year. Holiday calendars may vary by employee location. Employees should follow the holiday calendar assigned to their work location in the HR system.

Employees should book business travel at least 14 days before departure when practical. Airfare, hotel, and ground transportation should be booked through the approved travel tool unless an emergency, accessibility need, or customer requirement makes that impractical.

Managers approve travel before booking when the trip is not already listed in the department plan. Travel booked after manager denial is not reimbursable unless the denial is reversed in writing.

Sick Leave

Approval Requirements

Employees must receive manager approval before changing their regular work location. A temporary change within the same country for fewer than 15 business days may be approved by the manager. Longer changes require People Operations review.

Managers should consider team coverage, customer needs, time zone overlap, and data handling requirements before approving remote work.

rows.question: Are employees allowed to share passwords or MFA codes?
rows.answer: Employees must not share passwords, MFA codes, access tokens, or accounts. Each employee is responsible for activity performed under their account.

citations.citation_text: Employees must not share passwords, MFA codes, access tokens, or accounts. Each employee is responsible for activity performed under their account.

retrieved_chunks.content_preview:
Account Sharing

Employees must not share passwords, MFA codes, access tokens, or accounts. Each employee is responsible for activity performed under their account.

Sharing Rules

Employees may share data only with people who have a business need and appropriate access. Confidential and Restricted data must not be shared in public channels or with unapproved external recipients.

Sales materials may be shared externally only when marked as customer-approved or public-facing.

Prohibited Behavior

Employees must not attempt to bypass security controls, scan systems without approval, copy customer data to personal storage, or use company systems for illegal, harassing, or discriminatory activity.

Company Devices

Employees who regularly access company systems should use a company-managed device. Company devices must have disk encryption, endpoint protection, automatic screen lock, and current operating system updates.

Employees may not disable security tools or remove device management controls from company devices.

Personal Devices

Personal devices may be used for limited work access only when enrolled in approved mobile device management or when access occurs through approved browser-based tools. Personal devices must use a passcode, supported operating system, and automatic lock.

Restricted data must not be downloaded to personal devices. Confidential data should be accessed only through approved company systems.

Classification Levels

Northstar uses four data classification levels: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted.

Public data is approved for external sharing. Internal data is intended for Northstar employees. Confidential data includes customer business information, financial forecasts, non-public sales materials, and employee operational data. Restricted data includes secrets, credentials, regulated customer data, privileged security records, and sensitive HR case material.

Company Overview

Northstar Analytics builds analytics and workflow automation software for operations teams in finance, healthcare operations, logistics, and professional services. Employees are expected to protect customer trust, communicate clearly, and make decisions that improve operational reliability.

Northstar has offices in Toronto, Montreal, and New York. The company supports hybrid work and approved remote work across Canada and the United States.

Company Values

Northstar's operating values are clarity, ownership, evidence, and trust. Employees should make decisions with evidence, document important work, and raise risks early. Teams are expected to treat internal policies as source-of-truth guidance rather than informal suggestions.

Approved Use

Northstar systems must be used for company business, approved learning, customer support, and authorized operational work. Employees may use company devices for limited personal use if it does not interfere with work, create security risk, or violate policy.

Storage Rules

Internal, Confidential, and Restricted data must be stored in approved company systems. Restricted data must not be downloaded to personal devices. Confidential data should not be stored in local folders unless there is a documented business need.

Review Cycle

Northstar runs formal performance reviews twice per year: mid-year review in June and year-end review in December. Managers should collect evidence throughout the review period instead of relying only on recent events.

Performance Improvement Process

When serious performance issues continue after feedback, managers should consult People Operations before starting a formal performance improvement process. Documentation should include expectations, timeline, support offered, and review checkpoints.

Performance Documentation

Performance feedback should include specific examples, business impact, expected behavior, and follow-up actions. Managers should avoid vague labels and should distinguish between skill gaps, behavior concerns, and role mismatch.

rows.question: How quickly should employees submit expenses?
rows.answer: Employees should submit expenses within 30 calendar days of the transaction date. If expenses are submitted after 60 calendar days, manager approval and a Finance Operations exception note are required.

citations.citation_text: Employees should submit expenses within 30 calendar days of the transaction date. Expenses submitted after 60 calendar days require manager approval and a Finance Operations exception note.
citations.source: Source: FIN-001 Expense, Procurement, and Reimbursement Policy, Section: Policy Status

retrieved_chunks.content_preview:
Policy Status

This policy is effective February 1, 2026 and replaces the 2025 informal spend guidance. If an older team wiki or email thread lists a different limit, this policy controls unless Finance publishes a newer version.

Employees should submit expenses within 30 calendar days of the transaction date. Expenses submitted after 60 calendar days require manager approval and a Finance Operations exception note.

Reimbursement Timing

Approved expense reports are reimbursed in the next regular payroll cycle when submitted at least five business days before payroll close. Reports submitted after the cutoff move to the following payroll cycle.

Finance may hold reimbursement if the report lacks required receipts, approval, business purpose, or attendee information. The hold is administrative and does not imply misconduct.

Exceptions

Emergency expenses are allowed when waiting for approval would create a customer, employee safety, or business-continuity risk. The employee must document the emergency and obtain manager approval within three business days.

Recurring exceptions must be converted into a purchase order or department budget request. Finance does not approve repeated one-off exceptions for predictable monthly costs.

Expense Categories

| Category | Standard Limit | Approval Required |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Meals during business travel | USD 85 per day | Manager approval above limit |
| Customer-facing meals | USD 125 per attendee | Manager approval and attendee list |
| Office supplies | USD 300 per purchase | Manager approval above limit |
| Software subscription trial | USD 500 annualized value | IT review and manager approval |
| Conference registration | USD 1,500 per event | Manager approval before pu

Receipt Requirements

Receipts are required for every expense above USD 25. A credit card statement is not enough by itself when the merchant receipt is available. Missing receipts require a signed missing-receipt attestation that explains the business purpose, amount, date, and merchant.

Expense reports must include the business purpose in plain language. A report labeled only "meeting," "travel," or "miscellaneous" will be returned for correction.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Standard customer order form under USD 25,000 ARR | Optional unless redlines exist | Deal Desk | Sales Manager |
| Customer contract with security addendum | Required | Deal Desk | Sales Director |
| Vendor agreement under USD 10,000 | Required if data processing applies | Finance | Department Manager |
| Vendor agreement USD 10,000 or above | Required | Finance | Department

Prohibited Claims

Sales Representatives must not claim that Northstar guarantees revenue improvement, replaces all existing systems, meets every regulatory requirement, or has committed roadmap features. Customer names and confidential deal details should not be shared.

Approved Talk Track

Northstar helps operations leaders see where work slows down, which approvals are delayed, and which data quality issues affect business reporting. Sales Representatives should avoid promising product roadmap commitments.

Product Limitations

Northstar is not a replacement for a system of record, identity provider, ERP, or clinical decision system. Sales Representatives should not promise unsupported integrations, exact roadmap delivery dates, or customer-specific contract commitments.

Implementation Timeline

The typical implementation range is 6 to 10 weeks for standard deployments. Complex integrations or unusual data governance requirements may extend the timeline.

Working Hours

Standard collaboration hours are 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. local time from Monday to Thursday. Teams may define additional overlap windows when customer coverage or release coordination requires it.

Employees should keep calendars accurate and mark focus time when unavailable. Repeated inability to meet team collaboration expectations should be discussed with the employee's manager.

Northstar observes deployment freezes during payroll close, quarter-end financial reporting, and announced customer migration windows. The change calendar is the source of truth. Older release notes or team chat messages do not override the current freeze calendar.

Escalation Triggers

Escalate to a Manager when a customer reports suspected data exposure, repeated billing failures, executive escalation, blocked payroll or finance close, missed Enterprise SLA, or a production incident that affects more than one customer.

Escalate to Engineering through the incident channel when support can reproduce a product defect, a workaround is not available, or logs show repeated failures for the same customer workflow.
